walkthrough:
Clear the fraction by multiplying both sides by the denominator:
$$\tan\theta + 3\sin\theta + 2 = 2(\tan\theta - 3\sin\theta + 1)$$
$$\tan\theta + 3\sin\theta + 2 = 2\tan\theta - 6\sin\theta + 2$$

Collect all terms on one side:
$$2\tan\theta - \tan\theta - 6\sin\theta - 3\sin\theta = 0 \implies \tan\theta - 9\sin\theta = 0$$

Solve for $\theta$ in the first quadrant interval $0^\circ \le \theta \le 90^\circ$:
$$\text{From } \sin\theta = 0: \quad \theta = 0^\circ$$
$$\text{From } 1 - 9\cos\theta = 0 \implies \cos\theta = \frac{1}{9}: \quad \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{9}\right) \approx 83.6^\circ$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } \theta = 0^\circ, \quad 83.6^\circ)$$

ai_rubric.Solving Trigonometric Equations: Cross-multiplies to $\tan\theta - 9\sin\theta = 0$ (M1). Multiplies by $\cos\theta$ (M1). Factorises $\sin\theta(1 - 9\cos\theta) = 0$ (M1). Obtains $\theta = 0^\circ$ (A1) and $\theta = 83.6^\circ$ (A1).
